key_insight: Sparse SOS Layers integrate polynomial inequality certificates into learning while preserving the forward solver’s sparse structure during backpropagation.
engineering_relevance: They make certificate-based learning more practical for control, robotics, and optimization by reducing repeated-solve time and memory use.
method: Represent polynomial certification problems as differentiable SOS value layers.
Reuse the forward solve’s local sparse coordinates in the backward pass.
Keep the problem template fixed while learning objective coefficients, avoiding dense certificate construction.
evidence_signal: Across six application areas, tests report up to 2.7× faster total warm-call time and 1.7 versus 160 GiB memory for a tested dense parameterization; a design study reports zero certified violations on unseen instances and sizes with roughly 7× fewer solves than finite differences.
watch_item: The approach assumes a fixed template with learned objective coefficients; reported gains may not extend to changing constraint structures or other parameterizations.
paper_title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
